claims.claim: Up to 48 concurrent Lambda invocations can share one copy of a model in GPU memory.
claims.episode_span: Forty-eight Lambda calls now share one GPU model
claims.source_title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
claims.supporting_quote: Concurrent invocations in one environment share a single copy of the model in GPU memory, up to 48 per environment, and scaling follows GPU utilization, CPU utilization, and concurrency.

claims.claim: Lambda GPU functions are priced at the EC2 On-Demand rate plus a 9.75 percent management fee and $0.20 per million requests.

claims.source_title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
claims.supporting_quote: It is priced at the EC2 On-Demand rate plus a 9.75 percent management fee and the standard $0.20 per million requests.

claims.claim: At launch, Lambda GPU support covers G4dn, G5, G6, G6f, Gr6, Gr6f and G6e instances.

claims.source_title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
claims.supporting_quote: Event Functions running on Lambda Managed Instances can now run on EC2 G-series instances (G4dn, G5, G6, G6f, Gr6, Gr6f and G6e at launch)

claims.claim: Lambda GPU limits include 32 GB container images, 3 to 48 GB of accelerator memory, 15,000 vCPUs per capacity provider, and timeouts up to 90 minutes.

claims.supporting_quote: The limits are in the launch post: container images up to 32 GB, 32 GB of ephemeral storage, 2 to 32 GB of memory, 3 to 48 GB of accelerator memory, 15,000 vCPUs per capacity provider, and a timeout of up to 90 minutes for asynchronous and event source mapping invocations.
